anchor: DoPT’s Special Campaign 6 links workplace cleanliness with disposal of pendencies, records managemen
argumentsAgainst: Campaign-based drives may produce visible short-term cleanliness without sustained institutional change.
The source does not provide measurable outcomes, disposal quantities, compliance assessments or independent evaluation.
Digitisation and weeding of records require safeguards against accidental loss, unauthorised access and weak archival practices.
argumentsFor: Integrating cleanliness with pendency disposal addresses both physical workspace conditions and administrative efficiency.
Portal-based target uploading and progress monitoring can improve review, transparency and accountability.
Focused e-waste segregation can reduce unsafe disposal and support compliance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.
background: DoPT undertook a Preparatory Phase from 16 to 30 September 2026 across the Department and its Attached and Subordinate Offices.
The Implementation Phase was formally launched on 2 October 2026 and is scheduled to continue until 31 October 2026.
DARPG is identified as the nodal Department, while DoPT uploaded campaign targets on the SCDPM 6 portal for monitoring and review.
indiaImplications: Administrative efficiency can improve when pending VIP references, public grievances, parliamentary assurances and other time-bound matters receive targeted attention.
Better records management and digitisation can support continuity, retrieval and more organised use of government office space.
E-waste management brings environmental compliance into routine public administration.
The source does not establish actual nationwide outcomes, so benefits should be treated as intended or expected rather than demonstrated results.

bodyDimensions: Administrative reform: connect cleanliness with pendency reduction, records management and workplace productivity.
Governance mechanism: use target-setting, portal monitoring, time-bound review and responsibility allocation.
Environmental governance: segregate and dispose of e-waste under applicable rules.
Safeguards: protect records during digitisation and ensure that campaign activity becomes a continuing institutional practice.

officialFacts.text: The Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 was formally launched on 2 October 2026.
The Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 will continue till 31 October 2026.
The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) is the nodal Department for Special Campaign 6.
DoPT uploaded the requisite targets for Special Campaign 6 on the SCDPM 6 portal of DARPG.
DoPT focused on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

example.heading: Illustration: from target to institutional routine
example.text: Suppose a government office identifies pending public grievances, obsolete records and segregated e-waste during preparation. It may assign time-bound disposal responsibilities, digitise records selected for retention, use the campaign portal for progress review and continue periodic audits after 31 October. This is a hypothetical illustration, not a reported event.

pocketRead.excerpt: DoPT’s Special Campaign 6 combines cleanliness with pendency disposal, records management, digital governance and e-waste segregation, using targets and portal monitoring to support more efficient administration.

question.answer: The campaign can make cleanliness administratively meaningful by connecting it with time-bound disposal of pending matters, records review, space management and e-waste compliance. Its success would depend on measurable follow-up, record safeguards and continuation beyond the campaign period.
question.prompt: How can a cleanliness campaign become an instrument of administrative reform rather than a symbolic exercise?

sections.heading: From cleanliness to administrative efficiency
paragraphs: DoPT’s campaign treats office cleanliness alongside disposal of pendencies, records management, digital governance and better use of official space. The mechanism is to assess pending matters and records, formulate action plans, upload targets and monitor progress through the SCDPM 6 portal.

sections.heading: E-waste and institutional continuity
paragraphs: The campaign gives special attention to identifying, segregating and disposing of e-waste under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022. Digitisation and weeding can improve retrieval and space use, but the source does not report outcomes or explain the safeguards used to protect records during this process.

sourceTitle: DoPT Launches Special Campaign 6 with Swachhata Pledge, Cleanliness Drive and Tree Plantation on Swachh Bharat Diwas; Focus on Swachhata, Disposal of Pendencies, Records Management and E-Waste
staticDefinition: Administrative cleanliness is a governance approach that combines organised workspaces with timely disposal of pending matters, systematic records management, responsible resource use and accountable monitoring.
use: Use as an example of outcome-oriented public administration, linking Swachhata with e-governance, records management, civil-service efficiency and environmental compliance. Avoid presenting intended benefits as measured outcomes because the source supplies no evaluation data.

advisory_notes: The proposed GS2.5, GS2.8 and GS3.5 tags are broadly defensible, but the note should map them explicitly to governance, e-governance and environmental pollution rather than treating all three as equally central.
“Outcome-oriented public administration” is analytical framing; the source reports targets and activities, not DoPT-specific evaluated outcomes.
“Digital governance” and “civil-service efficiency” are reasonable implications, but should be presented as mechanisms or intended benefits, not demonstrated results.
The static definition of administrative cleanliness is an analytical construct, not an official definition; label it accordingly.
The claim that better records management can support continuity and retrieval is sound analysis, but the supplied release does not report achieved improvements.
The statement that campaign drives may produce only short-term cleanliness is a valid counterargument, not an established fact about Special Campaign 6.
The safeguards concerning digitisation, weeding, retention and unauthorised access are useful recommendations, but they are not described in the supplied release.
The hypothetical office example is clearly labelled as an illustration and does not fabricate a reported event; retain that label in revision.

wayForward: Convert campaign targets into recurring departmental indicators for pendencies, records retrieval, space use and e-waste compliance.
Maintain audit trails and retention safeguards during digitisation and weeding of records.
Continue portal-based monitoring and periodic review after the Implementation Phase ends.
Assess outcomes through transparent reporting rather than relying only on visible cleanliness activities.
